title: Scientists Trapped Antimatter for More Than 16 Minutes

scenes.text: Scientists held antimatter in a trap for more than 16 minutes.
Antimatter is the mirror twin of normal matter. When the two collide, they annihilate.
At CERN, the ALPHA team trapped atoms of antihydrogen so they never touched the walls.
In 2011 they held atoms for 1,000 seconds. Earlier trapping lasted a fraction of a second.
Since 2009 they've captured 309 antiatoms in total.
Sixteen minutes, for something that vanishes the moment it touches normal matter.

description:
In 2011, the ALPHA experiment at CERN trapped antihydrogen atoms for up to 1,000 seconds, more than 16 minutes.
Antimatter annihilates when it meets normal matter, so holding it for that long lets scientists study it. Since 2009 the team had trapped 309 antiatoms.
What would you want to learn from antimatter? Comment below.
first_comment: The trap held the atoms for 1,000 seconds, then the team let them annihilate to detect them. Would you want a closer look at antimatter?
